args: Chapter One
One Beautyfull Sunday
Ask Dad if you can go outside

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: One beautyfull sunday, Amy asked to go outside.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: Dad, can I go outside? Please? It's the most beautiful Sunday there has ever been!

args.speaker: Dad
args.text: No, it to Dangerous because of the huge rain forest.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: But Dad--

args.speaker: Dad
args.text: No buts, Amy. Nobody from the village ever goes near those trees. And besides... Sam is watching you.

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: By the garden gate, Sam the dog tilted his head and thumped his tail. He was ALWAYS watching.

args: Sneak out through the garden gate... quietly!

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: Hmph. 'Too dangerous.' I'll just have a tiny little look. What Dad doesn't know can't worry him...

args.speaker: Sam the Dog
args.text: WOOF!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: She tryed to go out side but thier dog Sam always brought her back in.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: Saaaam! Let go of my jumper! Fine. FINE. I'm going.

args: Wait for Sam to look away, then try the gate again

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: Okay. New plan. Tip-toes this time. Sam can't hear tip-toes. Nobody can hear tip-toes.

args.speaker: Sam the Dog
args.text: Woof woof!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: She tryed again but Sam brang her back.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: You are the best guard dog in the whole world, Sam, and it is EXTREMELY annoying.

args: Chapter Two
The Unexplored World
Sam is away at the farm -- cross the field to the rain forest!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: One day when her dog was out at a farm, Amy managed to get outside.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: No Dad. No Sam. Just me, the grass, and... oh my. THAT.

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: Then suddenly a dark forest loomed infront of her.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: The trees are like a giant wall... they're holding hands so nobody can get in. But look -- there's a little gap. Just my size.

args: Squeeze through the gap between the giant trees

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: She decided to explore the unexplored world. That's me. I'm the she. Here goes nothing...

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: As soon as she went in Amy saw it was a world parallel to thier own!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: It was a bautyfull paradise!

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: The colours! The flowers are singing... no wait, that's birds. no, wait. it might be the flowers.

args: Follow the glowing flowers deeper into the paradise
Chapter Three
So Many Animals!
Say hello to the maroon squirrel

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: Amy discoverd so many animals!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: Something maroon was hopping between the roots...

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: A squirrel! A MAROON squirrel! You're the colour of my nanna's favourite cardigan.

args.speaker: the Maroon Squirrel
args.text: And you're the first human I've ever seen! Are all of you this leafless?

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: You can TALK?!

args.speaker: the Maroon Squirrel
args.text: Everything talks on this side of the trees. You just have to come in and listen.

args: Find the orange fox

args.speaker: the Orange Fox
args.text: Ooooh, a visitor. I'm sorry about the squirrel. He says 'leafless' to everyone.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: You're the orangest fox I have ever seen. You look like a sunset with a tail.

args.speaker: the Orange Fox
args.text: Thank you! We take very good care of our colours here. The forest looks after us, and we look after the forest.

args: Meet the golden lion in the deep glade

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: A lion. A golden lion. Right. Be brave, Amy. He probably had a big breakfast.

args.speaker: the Golden Lion
args.text: Peace, little explorer. No one is eaten in the paradise. It is against the whole idea of a paradise.

args.speaker: the Golden Lion
args.text: You have seen our world now, Amy. When you go home... tell them what you saw. Tell them the truth about us.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: I will. I promise. Mum is NOT going to believe this!

args: Rush home and tell Mum everything!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: She rushed Home...

args: Tell Mum about the parallel world

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: MUM! The rain forest isn't dangerous, it's a paradise! There's a maroon squirrel and an orange fox and a golden lion and they TALK!

args.speaker: Mum
args.text: A golden... lion? That talks? Oh Amy. WAIT until your father hears about this.

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: ...and told her mum who told her dad who told the village.

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: But the village did not hear 'paradise'. The village heard 'LION'.

args: Chapter Four
The Giant Tree-Chopping Machine
The machine is heading for the forest -- stand in front of it!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: The village made a giant tree-chopping machine and they decided to chop down the forest because they thought it was a thret to humankind.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: No no no no NO. Not my paradise. Not my friends. MOVE, legs!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: Amy planted her feet in the grass, right between the whirring blade and the giant trees, and did not move.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: STOP! Everybody just... STOP!

args: Explain to Dad and the village why the forest must be saved

args.speaker: Dad
args.text: Amy! Get away from there, it isn't safe!

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: It IS safe, Dad. I've been inside. It isn't a threat -- it's a paradise, a whole world parallel to ours!

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: There's a squirrel the colour of nanna's cardigan, and a fox like a sunset, and the golden lion is GENTLE, Dad. Nobody is eaten in a paradise. It's against the whole idea.

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: You shouldn't be scared of the forest. You should be PROUD of it. We should take care of it!

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: Lukily Amy managed to stop them by staying in front of it just long enugh to explain to them that they should be proud of it and take care of it.

args.speaker: Dad
args.text: ...Proud of it. Well. I suppose it IS the biggest, greenest thing any village ever had.

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: They took her seriously and stoped.

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: The great machine rolled backwards, away from the trees, and its terrible blade went still.

args.speaker: Narrator
args.text: And from the very top of the giant trees, a maroon squirrel, an orange fox and a golden lion watched the girl who saved their world.

args.speaker: Dad
args.text: Alright, alright. But next time you explore a parallel universe, young lady... you take the dog.

args.speaker: Sam the Dog
args.text: Woof!

args.speaker: Amy
args.text: Deal.

args: The end ♥
Amy and the Rain Forest — a story by Clara
